experience.description: Tutored 15 first-year students in weekly programming workshops.
Built a microservice for internal billing using Java Spring Boot.
Maintained a Next.js marketing site and built React components.
Managed a £4,000 annual budget and organised six student events.
Supported 30 students through weekly Verilog lab exercises.
Co-authored a paper on low-power FPGA inference accepted at ICCAD 2026.
Built ETL pipelines processing 10M+ rows per day in Python and SQL.

jobs.title: Teaching Assistant - Data Structures and Algorithms
jobs.description: Support the delivery of CS201 by leading weekly lab sessions, grading programming assignments, and holding office hours to help students master core data structures and algorithm design techniques.
requirements: Minimum grade of A- in CS201 or equivalent
Strong proficiency in Java or C++
responsibilities: Lead one 2-hour lab session per week
Grade weekly programming assignments within 5 days

jobs.title: Teaching Assistant - Database Systems
jobs.description: Help students learn relational design, SQL, and transaction processing. You will mark coursework, run tutorials and support the final group project.
requirements: Grade A in CS301 or equivalent

jobs.title: Teaching Assistant - Introduction to Programming
jobs.description: Mentor first-year students taking their first programming course. Patience, clarity, and enthusiasm matter more than advanced expertise.
requirements: Minimum grade of A- in CS101
responsibilities: Provide pastoral support to new students

jobs.title: Teaching Assistant - Software Engineering
jobs.description: Assist the EBU6304 team-project module. Coach groups through requirements engineering, UML modelling, and agile delivery, and assess their deliverables.
requirements: Experience with Git, code review and CI/CD

jobs.title: Teaching Assistant - Digital Signal Processing
jobs.description: Support EE301 lab work in MATLAB and Python. Help students implement and debug DSP algorithms, and contribute to lab manual improvements.

jobs.title: Lab Assistant - Data Structures (Summer)
jobs.description: Summer-term lab support for resit students. Position is now closed but is retained for historical reference.

applications.coverLetter: Dear Dr. Turing, I am writing to express my strong interest in the Teaching Assistant role for CS201. As a third-year Computer Science student who earned an A in CS201 last spring, I am confident I can help students master data structures and algorithm design. I have prior tutoring experience and have built a small open-source data structures library in Java. Yours sincerely, Alex Johnson.
applications.aiSummary: Excellent fit: A in CS201, prior peer tutoring, strong Java background.

applications.coverLetter: Dear Dr. Turing, I would love to assist with CS201. Although my grade was B+, I have invested significant time outside class building data structures in Python and Java and I am eager to learn from you. Best regards, Bob Smith.
applications.aiSummary: Solid foundation but grade slightly below the typical bar.

applications.coverLetter: Dear Dr. Turing, as an MSc Computer Science student with a strong background in algorithms and software engineering, I would be glad to help support CS201. I previously TA'd a data-structures bootcamp at my undergraduate university. Kind regards, Sarah Lee.
applications.aiSummary: Strong MSc candidate but already at 18/20 weekly hours.

applications.coverLetter: Dear Dr. Turing, I am a final-year EE student who took CS201 as an elective and earned an A-. I have demonstrator experience for EE201 and I would value the chance to broaden my teaching experience into the CS department. Best, Diana Chen.
applications.aiSummary: Cross-department candidate with strong CS grade and prior teaching experience.

applications.coverLetter: Dear Dr. Turing, I am applying for the CS201 TA position. While my home department is Mathematics, I have taken three CS modules as electives and achieved strong results. I love explaining mathematical foundations of algorithms. Thank you for considering me. Best, Carol White.
applications.aiSummary: Strong mathematical foundation; particularly suited to algorithm proofs.

applications.coverLetter: I would like to apply for the CS201 TA role. Regards, Edward.
applications.aiSummary: Does not meet minimum grade requirement (C in CS101, no CS201 record).

applications.coverLetter: Dear Dr. Hopper, I would be delighted to support CS301. I achieved an A- in your module last semester and have worked extensively with PostgreSQL and MongoDB in side projects. Thank you, Alex Johnson.
applications.aiSummary: Strong CS301 result; first of three confirmed offers contributing to weekly overload.

applications.coverLetter: Dear Dr. Turing, I'd love to TA for CS101. I remember how intimidating my first programming module was and I want to make it easier for the new cohort. Best, Bob Smith.
applications.aiSummary: Good rapport potential with first-year students.

applications.coverLetter: Dear Dr. Hopper, I am writing to apply for the EBU6304 TA role. My MSc team project used Scrum, GitHub Actions and pair-programming, and I would love to share those practices with undergraduate teams. Sincerely, Sarah Lee.
applications.aiSummary: MSc candidate with real-world agile and CI/CD exposure.

applications.coverLetter: Dear Prof. Torvalds, I scored an A in EE301 and I have continued working on DSP through my research assistantship. I would be honoured to support next year's cohort. Best, Diana Chen.
applications.aiSummary: Outstanding EE301 grade; ongoing DSP research.

applications.coverLetter: Dear Dr. Turing, I would be happy to support CS101 as a TA. I tutored introductory programming last year and enjoy helping first-year students build confidence. Best regards, Alex Johnson.
applications.aiSummary: Strong CS101 fit, but combined with existing offers this pushes weekly hours above the 20-hour cap.

applications.coverLetter: Dear Dr. Hopper, I am pleased to accept the EBU6304 TA offer. My group project experience aligns well with mentoring agile teams. Thank you, Alex Johnson.
applications.aiSummary: Excellent SE background; third confirmed offer increases overload risk.

messages.content: Hello Dr. Turing, I just submitted my application for the CS201 TA position. Could you let me know roughly when shortlisting decisions will be made? Thanks, Alex.
Hi Alex, thanks for your application. We aim to complete shortlisting within two weeks. You will receive a notification on the platform as soon as your status changes. Best, Alan.
Hi Carol, congratulations on the offer for CS201 TA. Please reply to this message with your acceptance before Friday and we will get the paperwork started. Best, Alan.
Dear Dr. Turing, thank you so much. I am delighted to accept the offer. I will be in touch with HR this week. Kind regards, Carol.
Hi Diana, your EE301 TA interview is confirmed for 8 December at 09:30 in EE Building Room 2.10. Please come 5 minutes early. Best, Linus.
Hi admin team, the platform has been really easy to use so far. Small suggestion: could the dashboard surface upcoming interview dates more prominently? Thanks, Alex.
